meta.title: Where Does the Internet Live? | Nepal · Enhanced Learning

sectionText.data-center-basics: A data center is a building full of computers called servers. They store your photos, run your apps, and keep the internet working.
sectionText.nepal-dcs: Nepal has 9 data centers. 8 are in the Kathmandu Valley, and 1 is in Butwal. One of them is probably helping you right now, like when you check your bank balance or phone signal.
sectionText.always-on: Data centers run all day and all night, every day. They never stop. They use as much power as 128,000 homes — even while you sleep.
sectionText.power-bars: Nepal's 9 data centers use over 15 megawatts of power — enough for 128,000 homes. That is more than the whole city of Biratnagar uses, and five times what Dhangadhi uses. Just one row of server racks uses as much power as about 700 homes.
sectionText.water-usage: Data centers use water to keep their servers cool. Nepal's 9 data centers use about 230 million litres of water every year — about 90 Olympic swimming pools. This is the same underground water that people in Kathmandu drink.
sectionText.message-journey: When you send a message, it travels from your phone to a cell tower, then to a data center, and then to your friend. All of this happens in under 100 milliseconds — faster than you can blink.
sectionText.ewaste: Servers only last a few years. After that, they become electronic waste, or "e-waste." Old servers have toxic metals inside, like lead and mercury. Nepal has no official way to recycle them, so they often end up in landfills or get burned — which harms the environment.
sectionText.flip-facts: Data centers get very hot, so keeping them cool is a big challenge. They are also very secure, with fingerprint scanners and fences. Nepal's cool mountain weather actually helps keep them cool naturally. And they use millions of litres of water every day just to stay cool.
sectionText.map-location: 8 data centers are in the Kathmandu Valley, and 1 is in Butwal. Most of them are grouped together in the capital, handling most of Nepal's internet traffic.

pretrain.label: 🧠 Pretraining
pretrain.title: Key Terms to Know
pretrain.sub: Learn these words before we dive in — they'll help you build a mental model of how data centers work.

terms.def: A building full of computers (servers) that store data and run apps.
Uninterruptible Power Supply — a battery that keeps servers running during power cuts.
terms.hint: Bridges the gap before generators start

terms.def: Computer Room Air Conditioning — cools the servers so they don't overheat.
terms.hint: Uses water or refrigerant to remove heat

terms.def: A diesel engine that provides power during longer outages.
terms.hint: Can run for days if refueled

terms.def: The amount of data that can move through a network connection at once.
Discarded electronic equipment that contains toxic materials.

journey.title: Your Message's Journey
journey.sub: What happens when you send a message
descs: Your message starts on your phone.
It travels as radio waves to a cell tower.
The tower sends it to a data center in Kathmandu.
The data center delivers it to your friend.

server_rack.label: Server Rack
server_rack.desc: A standard rack of servers that store and process data.

cooling_unit.label: Cooling Unit (CRAC)
cooling_unit.desc: Keeps the room at a safe temperature for the servers.

ups.label: UPS (Battery Backup)
ups.desc: A battery backup that kicks in the instant power cuts out.

generator.label: Diesel Generator
generator.desc: A backup generator that keeps the lights on during longer outages.

network_core.label: Network Core Switch
network_core.desc: Connects every server rack together at high speed.

pdu.label: Power Distribution Unit
pdu.desc: Sends power from the UPS to each server rack.

fire_suppression.label: Fire Suppression
fire_suppression.desc: Puts out fires without damaging the equipment.

security_desk.label: Security & NOC Desk
security_desk.desc: Where staff watch over every system, all day and night.
